gaps.sentence: ___ feeling nervous, she delivered a flawless presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'In spite of' + -ing expresses concession with a non-finite form.

gaps.sentence: The ferry was cancelled; ___, we drove the long way round.
gaps.explanation: 'Consequently' introduces the consequence of the cancellation.

gaps.sentence: She took notes during the seminar ___ she could write it up that evening.
gaps.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of the action.

gaps.sentence: The drug is remarkably effective. ___, it has almost no side effects.
gaps.explanation: 'Furthermore' introduces an additional point supporting the same claim.

gaps.sentence: Demand for the vaccine soared; ___, production was doubled.
gaps.explanation: Soaring demand led to increased production: consequently marks the result.

gaps.sentence: She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: I'll take the job ___ they don't offer me any more money.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a future possibility that will not change the decision.

gaps.sentence: Scarcely had she opened the letter ___ she burst into tears.
gaps.explanation: 'Scarcely... when' marks the immediate consequence of the first event.
